bayts.text: Sulaymā (the world) set out to turn me from (my) merits, to lead my reins toward calamities.
She displayed, to snare my heart, the beauty of her splendour, and turned gifts toward me with courtesies.
She set about pleasing my soul so that I might incline to her, and tried to bend my heart toward the gifts.
She addressed me with words that invite one to seek her hand, and displayed truthfulness of promise with desirable things.
Now she comes to me and grants me her prizes, now she brings me glad tidings.
But I have known — and my knowledge shall benefit me — that she is false in her words.
The promises of ʿUrqūb (proverbial breaker of his word) are her model, and her promises are nothing but betrayals.
She shows no clearness without showing, after it, turbidity, and she turns about with snares.
Nor does she show benefit without having put harm into it, and she hides an injustice within her aid.
So I turned away from her toward that through which Allah brings me into Gardens holding faithful dark-eyed maidens.
They are the beauties whom Salmā, Hind and Laylā cannot equal among the maidens.
They are the beauties whom none wins but he who has adorned himself with God-fearing through acts of obedience.
They are the beauties who dwell forever in the pavilions they have amid the Gardens (Qurʾān 55:72).
Ḥūr with Allah, wide-eyed, whom neither menses nor filth approach: they remain ever pure.
Ḥūr with Allah, of equal age, sheltered beneath the domes, kept safe from misery.
They have surpassed the lamps in light; their fragrance is intense; they put to shame the full moon that appears above the heavens.
They have a tender, pure, fresh body; the light of (their) breast illumines the darkness.
Their bodies are a mirror for their spouses, yes, for the light of their bodies shames the lamps.
Since the Lord of the Throne created them, no blemish has touched them, in qualities or in essence.
And they seek no substitute for their spouses; and the radiance of light grows every hour.
And they never cease to be virgins with them (their spouses) forever: how noble they are, pure maidens!
And they come neither to death nor to old age, but remain forever abiding, loving.
They are the beauties in whom the heart has delighted: it prefers them to Salmā and the Hinds.
And their dowry is fear of Allah, their Creator, with repentance from the soul's passion (turning) to acts of obedience,
with repentance and submission to a King Who has bestowed the Chosen One, treasure of creatures.
I have surrendered myself to a Lord Who has no partner, together with him whose following is my occupation and my need.
I have surrendered myself to a Lord Who has no likeness, together with him whose love is the farthest of my aspirations.
I have surrendered myself to a Lord Who has no peer, together with him whose way is the best of roads.
I have surrendered myself to a Lord Who has no helper, together with him whose religion is the best of religions.
I have surrendered myself to a Lord Who has no beginning, together with him who has gathered the best of paths.
I have surrendered myself to a Lord Who has no end, together with him whose nearness is the greatest of my concerns.
I have surrendered myself to a Lord exalted above (any) son, together with him whose praise is my law and my habits.
I have surrendered myself to a Lord exalted above (any) purpose, together with him whose bounty is the most hoped-for of my treasures.
I have surrendered myself to a Lord exalted above (any) likeness, together with him who has been saved from every calamity.
I have submitted to Allah, Lord of the worlds, through Muḥammad, the best of those who have gone and those who will come.
May He bless him Who raised his degrees above all degrees, in the past and in the future,
and the Family, the Companions and those who hold fast to him, with the purest blessing, through which (He) banishes follies.
May He bless him Who raised him, exalted above those who have attained the highest stations,
and the Family, the Companions and those who follow his Sunna, with the purest blessing, through which I gather the openings.
May He bless him Who raised his prophethood, until the people of the prophecies sought refuge in him,
and the Family, the Companions and those who seek right guidance through him, with the purest blessing, through which I gather felicities.
May He bless him Who gave him a miracle that put to shame, every one, the sorcerers and the soothsayers,
and the Family, the Companions and those who seek succour through him, with the purest blessing, through which I gather wonders.
May He bless him Who made manifest his precedence over the whole assembly of the earth and of the heavens,
and the Family, the Companions and those who seek rescue through him, with the purest blessing, through which I gather outpourings.
May He bless him, with a blessing through which I may be upright, He Who singled him out with the drawing near (Qurʾān 53:8) in the meetings,
and the Family, the Companions and those who revive his Sunna, with peace, without end of limits.
That is the protector with whom I have sought protection from the evil of my soul, of Satan and of infirmities,
and from the schemes of enemies and from my time, and from speech and the evil eye, at all times,
and from the changing of my states toward other than guidance, and from all misfortunes and sins.
